blocks.content: An algorithm has linear time complexity if its execution time grows directly in proportion to the size of the input. In other words, if the input size doubles, the time it takes to run the algorithm roughly doubles as well.
If you were to plot this relationship on a graph, it would form a straight line — showing that the time increases at a constant rate as input grows.
Let's understand linear time complexity with the help of an example:

1def print_hello(n):
2    for i in range(n):
3        print("Hello")
4
5print_hello(5)

items: If n = 5, the function will execute 2 * 5 = 10 statements
If n = 88, the function will execute 2 * 88 = 176 statements
If n = 100000, the function will execute 2 * 100,000 = 200,000 statements

blocks.content: As we can see, the execution time of our code is directly proportional to the size of the input, hence, its time complexity is linear.
Linear time complexity is denoted by O(n).
